details: The crypto market experienced a sharp downturn on May 8th, with total market capitalization falling nearly 3.8% to around $2.61 trillion due to renewed military tensions between the United States and Iran. Bitcoin dipped below $77,000, and Ethereum dropped over 6%. This risk-off sentiment led to over $344 million in long position liquidations, pushing the Crypto Fear & Greed Index back into "fear" territory.
title: Crypto Market Dips Amid US-Iran Tensions, Over $344M Liquidated

details: The crypto market saw moderate gains on May 9th, with altcoins like ONDO (+33.5%), INJ (+12.4%), and VVV (+11%) significantly outperforming Bitcoin and Ethereum. This surge is attributed to strong narratives around Real-World Assets (RWA), DeFi, and AI. Institutional blockchain adoption is rapidly increasing, highlighted by BlackRock's tokenized money market funds and over $30 billion in on-chain RWAs.
title: Altcoins Surge, Led by ONDO, INJ, and VVV; Institutional RWA Adoption Grows

details: Prospects for US crypto legislation have improved, with the Clarity Act now having a 60% chance of passage following a Senate stablecoin compromise. However, a coalition of banking trade groups expressed concerns on May 8th that new language in the bill regarding stablecoin yield could disrupt traditional banking. The compromise bans direct yield on stablecoins but allows some rewards tied to account balances.
title: US Crypto Legislation Advances, Banking Industry Raises Stablecoin Concerns

details: Arthur Hayes, co-founder of BitMEX, stated at Consensus Miami 2026 on May 9th that 99% of altcoins could eventually drop to zero, describing this as a "normal market cleansing." He drew parallels to the S&P 500, where most companies ultimately fail, and noted that the 24/7 nature of crypto trading accelerates this process. Hayes suggested viewing tokens as software projects, many of which fail due to a lack of user adoption.
title: Arthur Hayes Predicts 99% of Altcoins May Fall to Zero in 'Market Cleansing'

details: Bitcoin's price has remained resilient above the $80,000 mark, supported by a stronger-than-expected US April jobs report that added 115,000 nonfarm payrolls. Furthermore, the US Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) expressed support for On-Chain Finance regulations is seen as a positive development for the broader cryptocurrency market. Despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, Bitcoin continues to be viewed by some investors as a potential hedge.
title: Bitcoin Holds Above $80K on Strong US Jobs Data and SEC Support
